_comment: SIGNAL ROLE CONTRACT. Vendored into every repo that produces runs.
JSON rather than YAML on purpose: this file is machine-checked from two
runtimes, and both read JSON with zero dependencies (Python stdlib json,
MATLAB jsondecode). The firmware repo is deliberately stdlib-only and has
no pyyaml; MATLAB has no dependable YAML reader. A contract that needs a
parser nobody has is a contract nobody checks.
Metrics and plot recipes address signals by ROLE, never by logged name.
This file is the role vocabulary and its per-source bindings.
If your copy disagrees with another repo's copy, that is drift. Run the
conformance check rather than picking a side.

roles.ref_cmd: the setpoint the error is formed against
roles.ref: trajectory-level reference upstream of the tracked setpoint; context on a plot
roles.err: tracking error; LOGGED not derived on the firmware sources, which makes it a free cross-check
roles.u_total: the command that actually reaches the plant; NOT the same physical quantity across sources
roles.pos: true vehicle position, Nx3 [x y z] NED; vector-valued, not three scalar roles
roles.pos_meas: ESTIMATED vehicle position, Nx3 [x y z] NED -- what the controller actually saw
roles.sp: commanded position, Nx3 [x y z] NED; the reference `pos` is scored against
roles.euler: measured attitude, Nx3 [phi theta psi] ZYX [rad]

sitl.column_format: NON-NORMATIVE -- NO CODE READS THIS KEY. Both resolvers hardcode the rule: a field name is prefixed with /uav/<BRANCH>/ UNLESS it already begins with '/', in which case it is a FULLY QUALIFIED column name and is used verbatim. See contract.column() in tools/mfcdata/contract.py and i_columns() in qsim/+qsim/contract.m -- the two must stay identical. Kept as documentation only; an earlier version of this string described a format the code did not implement and misled a reader into believing the prefix was configurable here.

SITL_6DOF_ANTON_MFC._note: SITL 6-DOF trajectory tracking, ANTON_MFC ONLY. Not a telemetry message and deliberately carries no `message` key -- it is a COMPOSITE of the NPS scope state (nps_scope.c), which spans four unrelated first path segments: TRUTH (simulator fdm), SP (guidance references), EST (state estimate) and WLS_U (allocator). One branch cannot prefix four segments, so every binding here is FULLY QUALIFIED. `mfcdata check` skips it (no message); `mfcdata verify` reports 'nothing to verify against' (no err role logged for these signals).

SITL_6DOF_ANTON_FINDI._note: SITL 6-DOF trajectory tracking, ANTON_FINDI ONLY. Structural twin of SITL_6DOF_ANTON_MFC: not a telemetry message and deliberately carries no `message` key -- it is a COMPOSITE of the NPS scope state (nps_scope.c), which spans unrelated first path segments: TRUTH (simulator fdm), SP (guidance references), EST (state estimate) and FLAT (the oneloop allocator). One branch cannot prefix several segments, so every binding here is FULLY QUALIFIED. `mfcdata check` skips it (no message); `mfcdata verify` reports 'nothing to verify against' (no err role logged for these signals). The ONLY difference from the ANTON_MFC branch is `u`: this airframe's allocator registers under /uav/FLAT/alloc/u/u_ (oneloop_findi.c / oneloop_fmfc.c), not /uav/WLS_U/u/u_ -- see note u_is_airframe_dependent_and_in_pprz_units.

SITL_6DOF_ANTON_FMFC._note: SITL 6-DOF trajectory tracking, ANTON_FMFC ONLY. Structural twin of SITL_6DOF_ANTON_MFC: not a telemetry message and deliberately carries no `message` key -- it is a COMPOSITE of the NPS scope state (nps_scope.c), which spans unrelated first path segments: TRUTH (simulator fdm), SP (guidance references), EST (state estimate) and FLAT (the oneloop allocator). One branch cannot prefix several segments, so every binding here is FULLY QUALIFIED. `mfcdata check` skips it (no message); `mfcdata verify` reports 'nothing to verify against' (no err role logged for these signals). The ONLY difference from the ANTON_MFC branch is `u`: this airframe's allocator registers under /uav/FLAT/alloc/u/u_ (oneloop_findi.c / oneloop_fmfc.c), not /uav/WLS_U/u/u_ -- see note u_is_airframe_dependent_and_in_pprz_units.

flight._note: Same firmware, same telemetry messages. Verified 2026-08-16: 40 columns across MFC_STAB and MFC_GUIDANCE present in both a current SITL capture and the fr_0003 flight export, none in only one. Kept as its own entry so a future divergence has somewhere to be recorded.

simulink._note: Roles are declared per scenario in +qsim/+scenarios/<name>.m as spec.signals.<role>. Only the vertical channel is established.

notes.ref_cmd_is_sp_traj: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against flight fr_0003, and it contradicts what the names suggest. The firmware forms its error against sp_traj_<axis>, not sp_<axis>: me - sp_traj reproduces the logged err EXACTLY (max difference 0.0000 across phi/theta/psi, 794 samples), while me - sp is out by up to 194% of the logged range on psi. An earlier version of this file had these the other way round on the strength of the names alone. Caught by the derived-vs-logged error check, which is the argument for keeping that check in every recipe with a logged error available.
notes.sp_is_unbound: sp_<axis> exists in the telemetry and is NOT bound to a role. It tracks close to sp_traj but is not what the loop scores against, and what it actually is has not been established. Listed under `unbound` so the conformance check knows its absence from `roles` is deliberate rather than an oversight.
notes.same_name_different_role: sp_traj appears on BOTH the Simulink and firmware sides and means something different on each: `ref` (upstream context) in Simulink, `ref_cmd` (the scored reference) in firmware. The role indirection makes this safe -- a recipe asks for ref_cmd and gets the right signal per source. But it means a cross-source comparison must NEVER be built by matching column names, however identical they look. Match roles.
notes.simulink_firmware_name_overlap: Five vertical-channel signals share names between Simulink mfc_z and firmware MFC_GUIDANCE: me_z, cmd_z, err_z, sp_traj_z, fk_z. Unsurprising if the firmware was ported from the model. A convenience for humans reading logs, not a mapping -- see same_name_different_role.
notes.u_total_semantic_mismatch: NOT a naming difference. Simulink u_total_z is total commanded force on the z axis; firmware MFC_STAB/u0..u3 are per-actuator allocated commands. Different physical quantities. A plot overlaying them would look reasonable and mean nothing.
notes.psi_is_unwrapped: On fr_0003 psi ranges to about -25 rad, so yaw is accumulated rather than wrapped to +/-pi. Any metric averaging or taking a max over yaw needs to know, and a comparison against a wrapped source would be meaningless.
notes.acc2att_is_a_simulink_block: The MFC_ACC2ATT branch is a 1:1 instrumentation of the accel_to_angle MATLAB Function block in models/controllers/mfc_quad.slx -- seven of its ten fields are that function's LOCAL variables (u1, vhatx, vhaty, cosphid, vhaty_cd, phi_d, theta_d), which have no output ports, so Simulink cannot log them without editing the block. Deliberately not bound. If ever picked up: the block takes roll from the x component and pitch from y, with the axis arrangement folded into R_psi = [sin psi, cos psi; -cos psi, sin psi]. That is not the conventional pairing -- verify against the firmware C rather than trusting shared field names.
notes.branches_use_different_references: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 and NOT guessable from the names. MFC_STAB forms its error against sp_traj_<axis>; MFC_GUIDANCE forms its against sp_<axis>. The two branches look structurally identical and are not. Evidence: on a SITL run, guidance me - sp reproduces the logged err to 1e-5 while me - sp_traj is out by 10.97. The FLIGHT log cannot settle this -- it was flown manually, so guidance was not driving and sp equals sp_traj there exactly. Two sources were needed to see it, which is the argument for running `mfcdata verify` against every source rather than the convenient one.
notes.sitl_6dof_is_fully_qualified: The SITL_6DOF_* branches are the reason the '/'-prefix escape hatch exists in both resolvers. Before it, the branch name WAS the first path segment, so all of a branch's roles had to live under one -- impossible here. Behaviour for every pre-existing binding is unchanged: none of the 22 bindings in contract v3 began with '/', so the escape hatch was a strict addition, not a change.
notes.sitl_6dof_frames_verified: NED throughout, z DOWN, no negation anywhere in this branch. TRUTH/* is fdm.ltpprz_pos (struct NedCoor_d); EST/* and SP/guidance/* are NED. The ENU->NED negation in pj_json_relay's FIELD_ALIAS applies to ROTORCRAFT_FP, and the only ENU source in the scope is SP/nav/*, which this branch does not bind. Empirically a climb drives sp and TRUTH z both more negative.
notes.sitl_6dof_sp_carries_a_hover_pedestal: SP/guidance/* is an ABSOLUTE NED reference carrying whatever hover altitude offset the run started from, whereas Simulink's pos_ref_log is absolute from zero. Any cross-source error comparison must subtract each leg's OWN first-in-window reference sample before the two error norms mean the same thing. The size of that offset is PER RUN and must be read off the file, not assumed: on mfc_sim_20260830_182223.csv it happens to be zero (sp and TRUTH both start at 0,0,0 and the commanded step is to (1, 1, -3) NED), so this capture does NOT exhibit the -2.008 m pedestal reported for an earlier one.
notes.u_is_airframe_dependent_and_in_pprz_unit: READ THIS BEFORE USING u FROM ANY FIRMWARE BRANCH. (1) AIRFRAME-DEPENDENT: the allocator output is registered under /uav/WLS_U/u/u_ by oneloop_mfc.c (ANTON_MFC) but under /uav/FLAT/alloc/u/u_ by oneloop_findi.c and oneloop_fmfc.c (ANTON_FINDI, ANTON_FMFC). It CANNOT be one shared binding, which is why these branches are named per airframe. All three branches now exist: SITL_6DOF_ANTON_MFC binds /uav/WLS_U/u/u_, SITL_6DOF_ANTON_FINDI and SITL_6DOF_ANTON_FMFC bind /uav/FLAT/alloc/u/u_, each verified against a real capture header (2026-08-30). (2) UNITS: firmware u is in PPRZ ACTUATOR UNITS (0 .. MAX_PPRZ; observed 0 .. 4082 on the 20260830 capture), NOT the normalised [0,1] of Simulink's alloc_u. u_rms, max_abs_u and du_rms from qsim.metrics.tracking_6dof are therefore NOT physically comparable to a Simulink run's -- they are a within-firmware magnitude only. (3) u_sat_frac IS INVALID ON ALL THREE SITL_6DOF BRANCHES AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED: the metric is mean(u < 0 | u > 1), which assumes the normalised range, so on pprz units it returns approximately 1.0 for any flying run. This is the role-level hazard u_total_semantic_mismatch already warns about, made explicit here because the number it produces looks like a plausible saturation fraction and is not one. (4) PRE-ARM SENTINEL ON THE FLAT/alloc BRANCHES: before the motors are armed, /uav/FLAT/alloc/u/u_* sits at -9600 (observed on the 2026-08-30 ANTON_FINDI and ANTON_FMFC captures, first ~2 s of every file, 3.8% of samples). In flight the same signals are ~1570..2400 pprz units. Any u magnitude taken over a WHOLE capture is poisoned by that sentinel -- window on the manoeuvre (the sidecar's t0_offset_s) before computing u_rms or max_abs_u.

unknown.units: Not established for any source. Firmware attitude fields are believed to be radians, unchecked against the message definitions.
unknown.frames: Not established. Models work in NED with z positive DOWN; recipes reverse the axis rather than negating data.
unknown.signs: NOT ESTABLISHED and the highest-risk unknown. The relay's alias step carries scale factors AND a frame negation. Matching field names between sources is NOT evidence that sign conventions agree.
unknown.sample_rates: Vary by source and run. Recorded per-run in the ingest sidecar, never assumed here. Some committed flight exports are low-rate ground-station exports wearing the filename a full-rate conversion would produce.
